source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's HOU3-HOU4 campus in Houston publishes 84 MW of IT capacity, the largest figure of any Texas facility mapped here, but it does not publish a rack density, so its AI relevance cannot be settled from the data.

The campus covers 347,000 square feet of technical space, about 242 square feet per megawatt. That ratio describes floorplan, not silicon. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 84 MW is roughly 2,100 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a traditional enterprise density, it is roughly 8,400. The gap between those two numbers is the difference between a campus built for AI and one built for general commercial tenants, and nothing in the published spec resolves it.

The one certification listed, Green Globes, is a whole-building environmental rating. It supports general occupancy, not any specific workload. No tenant, accelerator count, power procurement, or interconnection status is published, so the megawatt figure is a ceiling on what the campus could draw, not evidence of what it does.

Texas is the deepest market mapped here, with 137 facilities, but only 19 publish a megawatt figure. Those 19 total 475.41 MW, making this single campus 17.7 percent of all published Texas capacity. That share reflects disclosure as much as construction. Most of the state's mapped footprint is invisible in capacity terms, so an operator willing to publish a number can lead a ranking that does not mean what it appears to mean.
